title: Chapter 60: You’ve Found Another Murder Case?
html:
“You’ve found another murder case?” Inspector Lee sounded more than a little bewildered.

“Four years ago, a female student by the name of Zhang Ya jumped out of the building, but there is more to her death than suicide!” Chen Ge said firmly.

“Give me a moment. I’ll check the files. If the victim’s family requested an autopsy, we should have a record somewhere.” Without hanging up, Inspector Lee switched on the records-room lights and began searching. Five minutes later, he found something. “Wait—why does Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy sound so familiar? Xiao Chen, get out of that school now!”

“I’m already heading for the gate, what’s wrong?”

“There’s something wrong with that school. I can’t explain it in a few sentences, but I can give you one number: six people committed suicide there within two weeks, all under strange circumstances.”

Pages rustled over the phone as Inspector Lee searched the files.

“That sounds right! The number fits my theory.” The school gate had come into view. He was almost out.

“Fits what you’re thinking? What exactly is happening over there?”

“Never mind that. Check whether the first victim was named Zhang Ya.” Chen Ge needed to confirm his suspicion.

Inspector Lee checked the records twice before answering. “Yes, Zhang Ya. But the fall killed her, and the coroner found no other wounds. Police examined the scene that same day. She fell from the fourth-floor dance studio. The window was undamaged, and the soundproofing foam around it showed no sign of tampering or cleaning. We concluded that she jumped without anyone physically forcing her.”

“Without outside influence? Inspector Lee, have you considered that she was forced to do so? If she didn’t jump, she would have been raped!” Chen Ge relayed the scenes he had seen in the mirror.

“We considered that. The records include statements from Zhang Ya’s five roommates. All denied knowing anything. They said she jumped after class, when she was alone in the studio. According to them, she had always been under severe stress, kept to herself, and might even have been mentally unstable. The police interviewed the rest of the class to verify their accounts, and everyone agreed.”

“That isn’t who Zhang Ya was. They banded together to frame her!” Chen Ge burned with indignation on her behalf. He had not expected the entire class to turn against a girl who had done nothing wrong.

“Neither of us will ever truly know what kind of person Zhang Ya was, but the evidence doesn’t lie.” Inspector Lee could not understand Chen Ge’s agitation. “In any case, get out of that school now. We’re sending officers to bring you back.”

“They lied! Check Zhang Ya’s time of death. It should be before class ended. Those five girls falsified the timeline, which makes them accomplices!” Chen Ge’s voice rose despite himself.

“That’s where you’re wrong. Zhang Ya died between six and eight. The five girls left around 5:30, their usual departure time.” Inspector Lee did not know what Chen Ge had experienced at the school, so he assessed the evidence as an outsider.

“Impossible!”

“It is. The coroner estimated the time from livor and rigor mortis: between six and eight. The primary cause was a broken spine. She also suffered injuries to her skull, heel bone, and pelvis, all common in fatal falls.”

Chen Ge stopped, unable to refute the facts. “If Zhang Ya jumped before the five girls left, then the fall didn’t kill her at once. Her shattered bones left her helpless. She lay in her own blood, suffering in body and heart, until she finally died between six and eight.”

“That scenario is possible, but you’ve overlooked something. If she was still breathing, why didn’t the five girls help her? Even if they had some reason to leave her there, someone else at the school should have found her.”

“It was a holiday. The school was deserted except for the six girls practicing for a provincial competition. Their teacher had already left. Any guards could have been lured away by someone with bad intentions.”

“I’m not arguing hypotheticals with you. Whether Zhang Ya’s death was suicide or murder, you believe those five girls killed her and coordinated false statements. Yet all five died within two weeks. If your supposed killers are dead, how are we meant to investigate?” Inspector Lee cared more about Chen Ge’s immediate safety.

“I never said those girls were the murderers. They were accomplices! The true murderer is an overweight man about six feet tall with a stooped back!”

“That’s a remarkably detailed description. Care to explain how you reached that conclusion? Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy had no complete surveillance system four years ago, and every witness is dead. Now you tell me the real murderer remains at large. How do you expect me to believe you?”

The Ping An Apartments case had kept Inspector Lee working overtime for days, which was why he remained at the station at two in the morning. Weariness colored every word.

Chen Ge could discern the suspicion in Inspector Lee’s voice. “We can start by investigating the people who are related to Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy from four years ago; we have to find this person! He was at the crime scene!”

“Chen Ge, starting a police investigation is not a game. Do you know how difficult it is to reopen a case that was closed four years ago? Even if you can convince me, it’ll be pointless if you cannot convince my superiors. What we need is actual proof—not suspicion, not speculation.”

“Everything that I’ve said is the truth.”

“According to you.” Inspector Lee began returning the files to their places. “Why are you suddenly so invested in this case? You’ve never struck me as a young man driven by an overwhelming sense of justice.”

Why am I so insistent?Chen Ge was startled by this sudden question from Inspector Lee. He was reminded of the aid that Zhang Ya had lent him when he was trapped inside the wooden hut as well as the chilling loneliness coming from his back when Zhang Ya was standing behind him inside the dance studio.

“It’s nothing. As things stand, I’m the only person who can help her.” Chen Ge looked at the black phone.

“I still don’t understand you.” Inspector Lee paused. “But upholding justice is our job. Since you’ve raised these suspicions, I’ll personally look into them once we wrap up the Ping An Apartments case.”

“Thank you, Uncle San Bao!” Chen Ge breathed easier. “Catching the real murderer should give Zhang Ya some peace. As for this godforsaken place, I never want to come back.”

He hung up the phone and turned to look at Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy one last time.

To his shock, Zhang Ya, the Red Specter, was standing right behind him!

Three meters separated them. Fresh blood dripped from Zhang Ya’s school uniform as she studied him with her head tilted. This time, she did not approach. Something about her expression was strange.
